proposed_changes.progress: All four deferred safety-hardening items from the 2026-07-13 audit (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-13-playground-build-inspection-audit.md, line 71) are implemented directly (no builder dispatch needed — each item's scope was already fully pinned down by the ticket's file/line references, so implementing solo was faster than the coordination overhead of work orders). Item 1: upload.service.ts caps createPdfUpload at 5 MiB and reduces looksLikePdf to a %PDF- header-only sniff, dropping the whole-buffer stringify; report.route.ts maps the new 'pdf upload too large' message to 413. Item 2: telegram-bot.service.ts sendTelegramMessage now honors 429 retry_after via the existing fetchImpl seam plus a new injectable wait() seam, bounded to 3 attempts and a 30s max delay; non-429 failures still throw immediately. Item 3: /api/telegram/launch (telegram.route.ts) and /api/telegram/prefill (app.ts) now read x-telegram-init-data from the header, matching provider.route.ts's existing pattern exactly (clean cutover, no query fallback); apps/telegram-miniapp/src/lib/telegram.ts fetchLaunchContext sends the header instead of a query string. Item 4: init-data.ts splits the auth_date age check into a 300s past-age budget (unchanged) and a new 60s future-skew tolerance, throwing a distinct 'future-dated telegram init data' message; validateTelegramInitDataWithTokens now preserves either age-error message across multi-token retry instead of only 'stale'. All changes stayed within apps/api and apps/telegram-miniapp; no rori schema, migration, persona, or content changes.
findings: Item 1 scope decision: the pre-existing test 'rejects spoofed pdf uploads when bytes contain only a fake pdf header' (apps/api/tests/e2e/uploads-and-reports.spec.ts) encoded exactly the old whole-buffer-stringify behavior the audit wants removed — content starting with the literal %PDF- header would now pass the header-only sniff by design. Rewrote it to 'rejects uploads whose bytes do not start with the %PDF- header' using content with no %PDF- prefix at all, which still fails under the new sniff and preserves the required 'non-%PDF- bytes rejected' negative case from the acceptance criteria. This is a deliberate behavior narrowing called for by the audit, not a dropped test.

Item 4 required a caller-contract fix beyond init-data.ts itself: apps/api/src/modules/profiles/profile.route.ts (line ~36) and apps/api/src/modules/providers/provider.route.ts (3 call sites, lines ~86/150/205) each pattern-match on the literal string 'stale telegram init data' to return 401. Without adding 'future-dated telegram init data' to those same checks, a future-dated token would have silently fallen through to a 500 at every one of those routes. Added the new message alongside 'stale' at all 4 sites — same category of caller-contract wiring the brief called out explicitly for item 1's upload error, just not itself named in the item 4 file list.
telegram.route.ts and app.ts's prefill handler catch all init-data errors unconditionally and return 401 regardless of message, so no caller-contract change was needed there for item 4.

No existing apps/api/tests hit /api/telegram/launch or /api/telegram/prefill directly (grepped for the routes across apps/api/tests before changing the contract), so the header cutover in item 3 could not silently break a query-string-based test that already existed; new tests were added instead (apps/api/tests/telegram/launch-prefill.spec.ts) including one asserting a stale initData query parameter is now ignored (401) now that the header is authoritative.
risks: None identified for this cycle's scope. Out-of-scope items confirmed untouched: apps/api/src/modules/profiles/profile.route.ts's POST body-based initData contract (audit names launch/prefill only), rori wiki/persona content, TASK-011/TASK-012 adjacent deferral items.
proposed_decisions: Item 1 upload cap: chose MAX_PDF_UPLOAD_BYTES = 5 MiB (5 * 1024 * 1024) in upload.service.ts. Relationship to the 8 MiB Fastify bodyLimit (app.ts line 125, JSON body): 5 MiB of raw bytes base64-encodes to ~6.7 MB, leaving ~1.3 MB of headroom under the 8 MiB bodyLimit for the surrounding JSON envelope (filename, form fields, etc.), so an oversize upload reliably surfaces our deliberate 413 'pdf upload too large' rather than Fastify's blunt request-too-large rejection at the transport layer. Verified the existing 'accepts base64 pdf uploads above Fastify's default body limit' test (900 KB decoded) still passes well under the new cap.

Item 3 query fallback: chose a clean cutover (header only, no query-string fallback) over a temporary dual-read. Reasoning: the brief explicitly says to match provider.route.ts's existing pattern and 'not invent a second convention' — provider.route.ts has no fallback for its analogous header-only read, and adding a query+header dual-read here would itself be a second convention. The mini app and API ship from the same monorepo/deploy path with no evidence in this repo of independently cached or independently deployed mini-app bundles (no CDN-fronted static hosting found for the mini app), so the deployment-ordering risk the brief flagged (an old cached bundle hitting a new backend) appears low here. Added a regression test confirming the old query parameter is now inert (returns 401) so this is verifiably a hard cutover, not an accidental partial fallback.

Item 4 skew tolerance: chose 60 seconds for TELEGRAM_INIT_DATA_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SECONDS in init-data.ts, well below the existing 300s past-age budget. Reasoning: 60s comfortably covers ordinary unsynced-client clock drift (NTP-desynced consumer devices are typically within tens of seconds) while staying far short of anything that would meaningfully widen the replay window, and is consistent with common clock-skew allowances in adjacent auth ecosystems (e.g. 30-60s in JWT validators).

Item 4 multi-token loop: extended validateTelegramInitDataWithTokens to preserve either 'stale telegram init data' or 'future-dated telegram init data' across candidate bot tokens (previously only 'stale' was preserved), rather than letting a future-dated token degrade into the generic 'invalid telegram init data'. This is safe because the age check only runs after the HMAC signature already validated for that specific candidate token — a wrong token fails on signature mismatch before it ever reaches the age check, so preserving the age-error message cannot mask a genuinely bad signature from a different token. Covered by apps/api/tests/telegram/init-data.spec.ts.
